title: General constructible internal Hom and finite coefficient change
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, with $q$ a power of $p$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $n\geq m\geq1$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ and $B=A_{E,m}$, and use the quotient homomorphism $A\to B$. Work on either small site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ or $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with constant coefficient ring sheaves. Here $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ means bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude over $A$: there is a finite interval outside which $K\otimes_A^L F$ has zero cohomology for every sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules in degree zero. Write $T_B=T\otimes_A^L B$ for derived coefficient change, and $H_A(K,M)=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)$ for derived internal Hom.

For every $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the map
$$
v^{A,B}_{K,M}:H_A(K,M)\otimes_A^L B\longrightarrow H_B(K_B,M_B)
$$
is an isomorphism in $D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$. It is the unique transpose of coefficient change of the evaluation $H_A(K,M)\otimes_A^L K\to M$, under the canonical tensor comparison. It is natural in both variables and respects evaluation, tensor–Hom adjunction, and composition of internal-Hom morphisms. For $1\leq r\leq m$ and $C=A_{E,r}$ it satisfies
$$
v^{A,C}_{K,M}=v^{B,C}_{K_B,M_B}\circ\bigl(v^{A,B}_{K,M}\otimes_B^L C\bigr),
$$
using the canonical identifications of successive derived scalar extensions. These assertions hold for both finite coefficient sites, with their canonical site-comparison maps.

proof.text: Use the existing finiteHomDomain_endpoints theorem to put both etale endpoints in the required finite-Tor constructible category. proof.text: For arbitrary closed records, uncurrying identifies the specified base-change map with reduced evaluation. Naturality of the closed adjunction proves evaluation, uniqueness, naturality and preservation of arbitrary transposes. Strong monoidality from the site-descent square identifies reduced internal composition with the composite of the two reduced evaluations: expand composition, apply monoidal associativity and tensorator naturality, and use the two evaluation identities. These are ambient identities with no constructibility restriction.

source.place: Assembly of the unchanged coefficient-change theorem; proof step 2

proof.text: For successive scalar extensions, uncurrying their composite gives two inverse tensorators followed by successive scalar extension of evaluation. The tensor-composition square and naturality of the scalar associator identify it with the single reduced evaluation. Injectivity of transposition gives the actual Hom cocycle, with inverse associator in the contravariant input. On the etale site normalize the domain-calculus scalar square to the selected tensorators; on the intrinsic site use the separate intrinsic tensor-composition square.

source.place: Assembly of the unchanged coefficient-change theorem; proof step 3

proof.text: Build the composite tensorator for two functors by composing their natural isomorphisms. Apply the preceding transpose calculation to the two paths of the monoidal site square, then cancel the two input isomorphisms. This proves the ambient site Hom square with exactly beta inverse in the contravariant input, without assuming invertibility of Hom comparisons.

source.place: Assembly of the unchanged coefficient-change theorem; proof step 4

proof.text: Choose etale witnesses K prime and M prime for each intrinsic finite-Tor constructible input. The etale endpoint-domain statements descend by nu preservation. Compose the scalar/site isomorphism, the invertible site-Hom comparison and the witness isomorphisms to identify these descended endpoints with the desired intrinsic endpoints. Strict fullness of the intrinsic finite-Tor constructible property transports domain membership. The existing finite-Tor site square and the etale isomorphism make the intrinsic comparison invertible on etale witnesses by cancellation. Naturality conjugates it along the witness isomorphisms, proving invertibility on the original intrinsic pair.
